---
title: "Local Stress: Element-Wise Constraints with Percival Solver"
toc: true
---

## Description

This tutorial demonstrates local stress constraints in topology optimization.
Unlike global stress aggregation (p-norm), local constraints enforce stress
limits at every element individually. This provides stricter stress control
but requires handling thousands of constraints efficiently.

We use Percival.jl, a specialized solver for large-scale constrained
optimization, with continuation SIMP (penalty 1.0 → 3.0) to converge to
stress-constrained designs.

## Setup

```{julia}
#| output: false
using TopOpt, LinearAlgebra, StatsFuns
using StatsFuns: logsumexp
```

## Define the Problem

```{julia}
#| output: false
E = 1.0 # Young's modulus
v = 0.3 # Poisson's ratio
f = 1.0 # downward force
rmin = 3.0 # filter radius

problem = PointLoadCantilever(Val{:Linear}, (160, 40), (1.0, 1.0), E, v, f)
```

A fine 160×40 mesh (6,400 elements) tests the solver's ability to handle
many local stress constraints.

## Parameter Settings

```{julia}
#| output: false
V = 0.5        # volume fraction
xmin = 0.0001  # minimum density

x0 = fill(0.5, 160 * 40)  # initial design
N = length(x0)
penalty = PowerPenaltyFun(1.0)  # start with no penalization

solver = FEASolver(DirectSolver, problem; xmin=xmin, penalty=penalty)
stress = von_mises_stress_function(solver)
filter = DensityFilterFun(solver; rmin=rmin)
volfrac = VolumeFun(solver)
```

## Local Stress Constraints

```{julia}
#| output: false
comp = ComplianceFun(solver)
λ = 1e-4
# Minimize volume with a compliance regularization term. The regularizer
# steers the optimizer toward stiff layouts, preventing the trivial
# all-void solution that pure volume minimization would produce.
obj = x -> volfrac(filter(PseudoDensities(x))) - V + λ * comp(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))
thr = 150  # stress threshold

# Local constraints: (σᵢ - thr)/N ≤ 0 for each element
constr = x -> begin
    s = stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))
    return (s .- thr) / length(s)
end
```

Each element's von Mises stress must satisfy the threshold. The constraint
function returns a vector (one constraint per element), which Percival
handles efficiently using interior-point methods. The compliance regularizer
(`λ·uᵀKu`) penalizes overly compliant (near-void) designs, keeping the
optimization away from the degenerate empty-domain solution.

## Optimization with Continuation

```{julia}
#| output: true
alg = PercivalAlg()
options = PercivalOptions(; max_iter=10, subsolver_max_eval=50)
model = Model(obj)
addvar!(model, zeros(N), ones(N))
add_ineq_constraint!(model, constr)

x = copy(x0)
for p in [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]
    setpenalty!(solver, p)
    global r = optimize(model, alg, x; options=options)
    global x = r.minimizer
    println("Penalty $p: obj=$(obj(x)), max_stress=$(maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))))")
end
```

The continuation strategy (penalty 1.0 → 2.0 → 3.0) helps converge to feasible
designs by first solving a relaxed problem, then progressively penalizing
intermediate densities.

## Verify Results

```{julia}
#| output: true
@show maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x0))))  # initial max stress
@show maximum(stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x))))   # final max stress

# Verify peak stress doesn't exceed threshold by more than 5%
s = stress(filter(PseudoDensities(x)))
println("Stress constraint satisfied: $((maximum(s) - thr) / thr < 0.05)")
```

## Visualization

```{julia}
#| label: fig-local-stress
#| fig-cap: "Local stress-constrained design with element-wise stress limits (threshold=150)"
using CairoMakie
fig = visualize(
    problem;
    topology=r.minimizer,
    default_exagg_scale=0.07,
    scale_range=10.0,
    vector_arrowsize=0.5,
)

```

The optimized design shows smooth stress distributions without concentration
points, demonstrating effective local stress control.
